title: Mausoleum Of Job Charnock | Kolkata Trips
description: Visit the Mausoleum of Job Charnock in Kolkata. Learn its history, architecture, timings, entry fee, how to reach, nearby attractions, useful visitor tips.
textContent: Mausoleum of Job Charnock Hidden within the peaceful grounds of St. John’s Church, the Mausoleum of Job Charnock is one of Kolkata’s most historically significant monuments. It commemorates Job Charnock, an English East India Company administrator who arrived on the banks of the Hooghly River in 1690. Although modern historians continue to debate whether Job Charnock can truly be called the founder of Kolkata, his mausoleum remains an important symbol of the city’s colonial history and one of the oldest British funerary monuments in India. Today, the monument forms an essential stop on heritage walks through the historic B.B.D. Bagh area. History of the Mausoleum of Job Charnock Job Charnock served the English East India Company for many years in Bengal. After moving the Company’s trading settlement to Sutanuti in August 1690, he spent the last years of his life there. He died on 10 January 1693. Initially, Charnock was buried at the burial ground that later became the site of St. John’s Church. Around 1695, his son-in-law Charles Eyre, who succeeded him as the Company’s chief in Bengal, commissioned the construction of the mausoleum in his memory. The monument predates St. John’s Church itself by nearly a century, making it one of Kolkata’s oldest surviving European structures. Was Job Charnock Really the Founder of Kolkata? For generations, Job Charnock was popularly regarded as the founder of Kolkata. However, extensive historical research has shown that the villages of Sutanuti, Govindapur, and Kalikata existed long before Charnock’s arrival. In 2003, the Calcutta High Court ruled that no single individual could be officially recognized as the founder of Kolkata. Despite this, Job Charnock remains one of the most influential early British administrators associated with the city’s development, and his mausoleum continues to be an important historical landmark. Architecture and Design of Mausoleum of Job Charnock The Mausoleum of Job Charnock is an excellent example of early Indo-European funerary architecture. Notable architectural features include: Octagonal floor plan Elegant stone dome Thick stone pillars supporting the roof Charnock’s stone tomb at the centre Beautifully carved memorial tablets Simple yet dignified Mughal-inspired design The mausoleum was constructed using Gaur stone, a durable black basalt transported from the ruins of the medieval city of Gaur in present-day West Bengal and Bangladesh. Its restrained elegance reflects the early colonial style before elaborate Victorian architecture became common in Kolkata. Historical Significance of Mausoleum of Job Charnock The mausoleum is significant for several reasons: One of Kolkata’s oldest surviving monuments Among the earliest British memorials in India Associated with the beginning of British commercial expansion in Bengal Part of the heritage complex of St. John’s Church An important stop on Kolkata heritage walks The monument offers valuable insight into the early years of the East India Company’s presence in eastern India. Timings of Mausoleum of Job Charnock The mausoleum can be visited during the opening hours of St. John’s Church. Opening Hours Monday to Saturday: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM Sunday: Limited access during church services Visitors are advised to arrive before late afternoon to explore the church grounds comfortably. Entry Fee of Mausoleum of Job Charnock The mausoleum is located within the St. John’s Church complex. Approximate Entry Charges Indian Visitors: ₹10 Foreign Visitors: ₹10 Charges may change over time. Best Time to Visit in Mausoleum of Job Charnock The ideal time to visit is between October and March, when Kolkata enjoys pleasant weather. Morning visits offer: Comfortable temperatures Better photography Fewer visitors Peaceful surroundings Combining the visit with nearby colonial landmarks makes for an enriching half-day heritage tour. How to Reach the Mausoleum of Job Charnock By Metro The nearest metro stations are: Esplanade Mahakaran (East-West Metro, depending on service availability) Both stations are within walking distance or a short taxi ride. By Taxi Taxis and app-based cabs are readily available throughout Kolkata. By Bus Several public buses connect B.B.D. Bagh with different parts of Kolkata. By Ferry Visitors may also arrive via the nearby ferry terminals across the Hooghly River and continue by taxi or on foot. Dress respectfully as the monument is within a church compound. Photography is generally permitted outdoors; check for restrictions inside. Spend time exploring the church cemetery and surrounding monuments. Hire a knowledgeable guide for deeper historical insights. Carry drinking water during warmer months. Combine your visit with a heritage walk around Dalhousie Square (B.B.D. Bagh). Why Visit the Mausoleum of Job Charnock? Whether or not Job Charnock deserves the title of Kolkata’s founder, his mausoleum remains one of the city’s most fascinating historical landmarks. It tells the story of the early days of the British East India Company, the emergence of colonial Calcutta, and the complex history that shaped modern Kolkata. For history lovers, architecture enthusiasts, photographers, and heritage travellers, the Mausoleum of Job Charnock offers a quiet yet deeply meaningful glimpse into more than three centuries of Kolkata’s past. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Where is the Mausoleum of Job Charnock located? It is situated inside the historic St. John’s Church compound in B.B.D. Bagh, Kolkata. 2. Who was Job Charnock? Job Charnock was an English East India Company official associated with establishing the Company’s settlement at Sutanuti in 1690. 3. Why is the mausoleum famous? It is one of Kolkata’s oldest colonial monuments and the burial place of Job Charnock. 4. When was the mausoleum built? It was constructed around 1695 by Charles Eyre after Job Charnock’s death. 5. Is Job Charnock officially the founder of Kolkata? No. The Calcutta High Court ruled in 2003 that no single individual can officially be called the founder of Kolkata. 6. What is the architectural style of the mausoleum? It combines early colonial design with Mughal-inspired architectural elements and features an octagonal plan with a stone dome. 7. What are the visiting hours? Generally, it is open during St. John’s Church visiting hours, typically from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays. 8. Is there an entry fee? Yes. Entry is through the St. John’s Church complex, which charges a nominal admission fee. 9. What are the nearby attractions? Visitors can also explore St. John’s Church, Raj Bhavan, Writers’ Building, GPO, Town Hall, High Court, B.B.D. Bagh, and Howrah Bridge. 10. How much time should I spend here? Most visitors spend 30 to 45 minutes exploring the mausoleum and the surrounding church grounds. 11. Can photography be done at the mausoleum? Photography is usually allowed in the outdoor areas, though visitors should follow any rules displayed by the church authorities. 12. What is the best season to visit? The winter months from October to March offer the most comfortable weather for sightseeing. 13. Can the mausoleum be included in a heritage walk? Yes. It is a key stop on many Kolkata heritage walks covering the colonial district and B.B.D. Bagh. 14. Why is the Mausoleum of Job Charnock important? It preserves the memory of one of the earliest English East India Company officials in Bengal and represents an important chapter in Kolkata’s colonial history. 15. Is the Mausoleum of Job Charnock suitable for families and students? Yes. It is an excellent educational destination for anyone interested in Indian history, colonial architecture, and Kolkata’s heritage.
